5.text: At 5%, 17 of 20 buildings get built, adding 2,280 new homes, but only 117 are affordable, 24 fewer than at 10%. A household that qualifies has odds of 1 in 284 from these 20 buildings, and about 45 affordable homes would go to women-led households. Of 100 women-led renter households, only 16 qualify: 41 earn too little and 43 earn too much, though 9 of those still spend 30% or more on rent.

8.text: At 8%, 15 of 20 buildings get built, making 1,850 new homes, 148 of them affordable, with about 57 going to women-led households. Even for a household that qualifies, there are too few homes: the odds are 1 in 225 from these 20 buildings. Of 100 women-led renter households, only 16 qualify. 43 earn too much (9 still spend 30%+ on rent) and 41 earn too little.

10.text: At 10%, 13 of 20 buildings get built (an illustrative estimate), creating 1,400 new homes, 141 of them affordable, and about 54 would go to women-led households. Of 100 women-led renter households, only 16 qualify, with odds of 1 in 236 from these 20 buildings. The other 43 earn too much, though 9 of them still spend 30%+ of income on rent, and 41 earn too little.

20.text: At 20%, only 6 of 20 buildings get built, making 48 affordable homes, compared with 141 at 10%. About 18 would go to women-led households, and a qualifying household's odds are 1 in 693 from these 20 buildings. Of 100 women-led renter households, only 16 qualify. 43 earn too much (9 of them still spend 30%+ of income on rent), and 41 earn too little.
